# Pragma Research: company, product and research source map

## Company

Cadence is a deep real-time brain that learns from experience. Pragma Research's ambition is to supply brains for robots that keep improving throughout their working lives. Pragma Research builds the brains; robot manufacturers build the bodies.

The company is seeking robotics evaluation partners and investors. The proposed commercial path starts with a paid evaluation on a concrete adaptation or recovery task, followed by a supported runtime and embodiment license, and expansion across robots and tasks. The proposed financing target is $4 million over 18 months for physical proof, a paid evaluation and repeatable integration. These are plans rather than achieved customer or financing outcomes.

## Cadence architecture

The technical contribution is recursive state-and-error observation within one coupled settling and learning architecture. Bounded observer-like, self-reading software patches hold local state and records, communicate through ports, read states and prediction errors, and contribute feedback or repair. Observer populations can themselves be observed. The jointly settled state supplies the answer.

Cortex and Brain expose a shared mathematical substrate. The runtime jointly settles represented state, recomputing exact prediction errors with analytic derivatives and a global energy check. Numerical settling energy is an objective function, not electrical energy in joules. The biological hypothesis is inspired by cortical cooperation; software behavior alone does not establish that a human cortical column implements these equations.

Deep refers to recursively coupled processing and observer populations. Real-time describes participation in an ongoing observation/action loop, with decision rates measured for each body and workload. Hard deadlines, useful depth advantages and broad skill retention need their own evidence.

The open-source core requires Python 3.11 or later, has no mandatory runtime dependencies and is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Optional accelerated paths have additional requirements. Consult the repository and package release for exact implementation details and licensing.

- Repository: https://github.com/muellerberndt/cadence

## Interactive architecture illustration

https://floatingpragma.io/cadence/#inside-the-brain lets visitors change a sensory signal, choose zero to two observer levels, inspect patch state/prediction/error, and step through a bounded settlement. Six scalar patches at maximum depth use fixed illustrative weights, exact error derivatives and a positive activity penalty. The forward reference uses the same relations by forward substitution. The illustration explains computation; it is not a trained brain, a performance benchmark or the full Cadence runtime. Query settlement changes activity; learning can also change relation parameters.

## Experimental evidence

Two selected Cadence agents achieved 63/64 and 64/64 successes in separate reserved ViZDoom Basic evaluations, compared with original founder baselines of 61/64 and 53/64 respectively. Both improved native return. The first success-rate difference itself was not established. Each set of 64 seeds had 60 distinct initial frames. Training used finite teaching, simulator-assisted counterfactual practice, replay and candidate selection. The second candidate changed the replay setting as well as receiving further experience. These are single-room results, not evidence of general Doom play or a causal benefit from recursive depth.

Doom evidence excerpt: https://floatingpragma.io/evidence/cadence/doom-confirmations.json

CartPole evaluation covered three layouts and three model initializations. All 180 held-out episodes reached the 500-step limit; no actions were refused across 90,000 decisions. Training used 128 supplied state/action examples per model and full numerical observations. No teacher selected evaluation actions. A single patch also solved the task. The result establishes bounded supervised control rather than reward-only discovery or a depth advantage.

CartPole evidence excerpt: https://floatingpragma.io/evidence/cadence/cartpole-confirmations.json

The first-party JSON files are compact projections of source records. They preserve original source hashes, outcomes and experimental conditions. The Doom excerpt includes existing independent verification records. These excerpts do not include all checkpoints and are not complete reproduction bundles. The public demo-code repository is a separate code surface; do not assume its branch includes every local experimental artifact summarized here.

## Proposed physical demonstration

The first proposed robotics demonstration is a small rover compensating when one wheel's motion response changes. Ordinary odometry and action feedback supply the experience. Compare recovery with frozen Cadence and competent adaptive and neural baselines under matched information and resource budgets. Restore the original body condition to measure retained performance separately from relearning. Success has to be established before a physical pilot is claimed.

The deployment programme measures useful task completion, interventions, recovery experience, retained behavior, end-to-end latency, learning cost and electrical energy. Broad robot competence, persistent skill retention and low-energy operation remain goals.

## OPH research origin

Observer Patch Holography explores whether bounded observers can form a shared physical account through local records, overlap comparison and repair. An observer-like self-reading system has bounded local state, ports or boundaries, readback, records, feedback or repair moves, and an inspectable evidence bundle.

The research develops explicit finite constructions and conditional mathematical implications connecting record agreement to quantum probability, geometry, gauge structure and gravitational dynamics. Formal proofs establish consequences of the stated assumptions. Reproducible simulations test the declared models. Whether nature realizes those structures requires physical identification and discriminating measurements. Numerical matches using measured targets are diagnostics.

## Three settlement design patterns

Flat settlement reads supplied sensors; ordinary state-coupled settlement adds learned intermediate states; recursive observer settlement adds exact prediction-error readback. All three share the patch/repair law, learning API and final qualification. Choose a layout by measured task quality, query latency and learning cost.
